nodes.norm_label: payments.refund_status walks processing -> completed or failed, with the stripe error appended to refund_reason on failure

nodes.norm_label: document loaders take the tenant's currency_code, so embedded text renders money in the tenant's own currency rather than a hardcoded $

nodes.norm_label: pgrst116 on the source row means it was deleted after the queue trigger fired, so the item is treated as a delete rather than an error

nodes.norm_label: six-hourly sweep that reconciles every non-terminal deposit hold in the database against the truth at stripe

nodes.label: PRINCIPLE 1 — record-anchored: the hold is read with the account, mode and platform it was CREATED under, never the tenant's current values, because wrong-platform keys make Stripe report the PI as missing, which looks exactly like an expired hold
nodes.norm_label: principle 1 — record-anchored: the hold is read with the account, mode and platform it was created under, never the tenant's current values, because wrong-platform keys make stripe report the pi as missing, which looks exactly like an expired hold

nodes.label: PRINCIPLE 2 — fail safe, never open: anything inconclusive leaves the row exactly as it is; no state that would allow a second authorisation is ever written on a guess, and no authorisation is cancelled without proving it is an orphan
nodes.norm_label: principle 2 — fail safe, never open: anything inconclusive leaves the row exactly as it is; no state that would allow a second authorisation is ever written on a guess, and no authorisation is cancelled without proving it is an orphan

nodes.label: A row saying 'held' is never demoted on an inconclusive read: place-deposit-hold, create-hold-checkout, cancel-rental-refund, deduct-from-deposit and sync-deposit-hold all key on the literal 'held', so demoting would unblock a second authorisation AND stop the release path at once
nodes.norm_label: a row saying 'held' is never demoted on an inconclusive read: place-deposit-hold, create-hold-checkout, cancel-rental-refund, deduct-from-deposit and sync-deposit-hold all key on the literal 'held', so demoting would unblock a second authorisation and stop the release path at once

nodes.label: PRINCIPLE 3 — expiry provenance: deposit_hold_expires_at is only ever written from a real capture_before, because resolveHoldExpiry's now+7d fallback MOVES on every call and would re-arm the clock so a reconciled rental could never enter the refresh window
nodes.norm_label: principle 3 — expiry provenance: deposit_hold_expires_at is only ever written from a real capture_before, because resolveholdexpiry's now+7d fallback moves on every call and would re-arm the clock so a reconciled rental could never enter the refresh window

nodes.label: EC-23: never insert a payments row, not even for a hold Stripe reports as captured — backfilling payments keyed on a deposit-hold PaymentIntent arms the rental-cancellation path on every rental it touches
nodes.norm_label: ec-23: never insert a payments row, not even for a hold stripe reports as captured — backfilling payments keyed on a deposit-hold paymentintent arms the rental-cancellation path on every rental it touches

nodes.label: Compare-and-set on BOTH the status read AND the PaymentIntent probed: the refresh engine can cancel PI_A and install a live PI_B under the same 'held' status, so a status-only CAS would stamp 'expired' over a live authorisation
nodes.norm_label: compare-and-set on both the status read and the paymentintent probed: the refresh engine can cancel pi_a and install a live pi_b under the same 'held' status, so a status-only cas would stamp 'expired' over a live authorisation

nodes.norm_label: the only reaper of rows stranded in a claim state (processing / refreshing / capturing) by a crash, a timeout or a mid-flight deploy — 30 minutes stale, with a recent deposit_hold_links row as the stronger liveness signal

nodes.norm_label: orphan sweep a: a deposit_hold_links row still 'pending' an hour later belongs to a writer that died — if its paymentintent is live and is not the rental's current hold, it is a renter's money held twice

nodes.norm_label: orphan sweep b: superseded paymentintents still at requires_capture, keyset-paginated oldest-first over the whole lookback with ledger markers, because a desc limit(40) query re-reads the newest page forever and the orphans that matter are the old ones

nodes.norm_label: a cancelled paymentintent is not always a network expiry: cancellation_reason 'requested_by_customer' or deposit_hold_release_requested_at means a human asked, so the row records 'released' rather than a silent 'expired'

nodes.norm_label: verify_jwt=false, so the only gate is in this file: either the pg_cron x-platform-secret validated by platform_verify_secret(), or a super-admin user jwt resolved through app_users

nodes.norm_label: deploy order matters: net.http_post is asynchronous, so a 401 lands in net._http_response and never in cron.job_run_details — a cron sending the wrong credential looks perfectly healthy while nothing is reconciled
